title: Prepare Luxforge v0.1.0 for distribution
objective: Prepare macOS Apple silicon and Linux x86-64 downloads together, matching source, distribution policy, macOS signing/notarization, native qualification and one reviewable joint release packet without publishing it.
context_summary: The owner requested preparation and chose macOS and Linux together on 2026-10-08. Targets are aarch64-apple-darwin and the existing x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu Ubuntu 24.04/glibc 2.39 baseline; Windows remains later scope. Both platform gates must pass before the joint release is ready. Paid Apple Developer Program membership is active, verified read-only on 2026-10-09. The owner reports completing signing setup with the local notarization Keychain profile luxforge-notarization; identity/private-key usability and profile authentication remain unverified until the final candidate task; preparation does not authorize credential creation or acceptance of further agreements. Operator setup is documented in the design. Routine code organization, icon, archive/desktop integration and manifest representation are delegated within the design. Current-format-only rules remain; no migrations, dist-profile dependency, stores/updater or feature-roadmap prerequisites. Use the roadmap high-tier model minimum and re-review current main. Signing credentials, complete owner RAW manifest, macOS floor machine, native x86-64 Linux GPU/Wayland/X11 machine and explicit foreground installation sessions are late qualification inputs, not dependencies of independent tooling. Preparation does not authorize creating or pushing a tag. The owner explicitly chose automatic pre-release publication when they push a release tag. Existing IDs are preserved; Linux and combined-release outputs are appended. The owner subsequently authorized tag-triggered build implementation: normalized tag versions override the developer workspace version without modifying source/lock. Versioned candidate packaging, optional signing, transport verification and automatic GitHub pre-release publication are delivered under the tag-build design; broad distribution acceptance remains incomplete.

tasks.description: Unify application and candidate identity for the editor, both CLIs and release metadata.
extra_context: Ordinary developer builds use workspace.package.version; release builds use the validated normalized tag as the shared compiled application version without rewriting manifests or lockfile. Keep format markers independent. A numeric macOS build number is owned by packaging metadata.

Add non-launching --version to luxforge and luxforge-json and reuse luxforge-ctl behavior. No catalog/data root or GUI launch is needed. Any service-visible addition uses the shared schema/command service.

Define candidate identity and the outside-bundle release.json contract for later tasks: full revision, version, build number, target, profile, toolchain/SDK/native compiler, lock hash, final artifacts and executable hashes, source identity, signing/notary and qualification statuses. Avoid self-referential hashes.
Release input validation refuses dirty tracked/untracked sources, mismatches, unsupported targets and reused outputs. Development packaging remains explicitly unsigned and may record a dirty tree.

Candidate validation admits only the two shipping targets; per-target build/executable/signing/evidence records share the same commit/version/lock. Linux Apple signing/notary fields are not applicable; macOS requirements cannot be bypassed by a Linux result.

Tag identity and all three --version paths are implemented. Complete any remaining final-distribution build-environment/source/qualification metadata; do not require a Cargo version bump for every release tag.

tasks.description: Assemble complete corresponding source and audit-ready notices with an offline rebuild check.
extra_context: Reuse the existing inventory/native/font/theme/data/Lensfun notice collectors. Review runtime-used licences and native static linking, selected licences, patches and LGPL modification/relinking requirements; prepare a factual review artifact without claiming an audit from inventory.

Generate a source archive from an exact clean revision with vendored Rust crates, bundled native sources/patches, required compiled-in assets, licence texts and build/install/relink instructions. Preserve Cargo aliases/deployment configuration while adding offline source replacement.

Private originals, the licensed sample corpus, catalogs/secrets, caches, local paths and verification data are excluded. Explicitly document test-only omissions; do not omit any source needed to build the shipped product.

The source packer can be built independently of application-version changes and macOS selection; final archive naming uses the candidate identity. A GitHub repository auto-archive alone is insufficient.

tasks.description: Produce a fresh distribution-specific advisory disposition for the frozen dependency graph.
extra_context: The current paste reason says local S0 development only; ttf-parser explicitly says no distribution approval. Neither current suppression may be reused as evidence of distribution suitability.

Recheck primary upstream advisories/releases for the exact shipping graph. Remove an exception through a compatible pinned update where available, or record the current exposure and a narrowly bounded distribution disposition with review/expiry; do not replace the GUI stack or create a private fork solely for a maintenance advisory.

If a public-risk decision cannot be supported by the reviewed evidence or existing authorization, record that unresolved publication blocker in the disposition. Do not suppress the finding, extend expiry automatically or hold up source/packaging/verifier work.
Keep development audit enforcement and its existing advisory tracking consistent. This task produces evidence and policy; it is not an approval/request task.

Review may run alongside version/source preparation: record the reviewed input lock hash and shipping dependency graph. Final assembly verifies graph equality and binds the disposition to the frozen candidate lock hash; any dependency/source/feature change invalidates the disposition and needs a fresh review.

extra_context: Reuse existing release build and development packaging collectors; add an explicit release path, never alter development packaging into implicit signing/submission.

tasks.description: Implement explicit Developer ID signing, notarization and stapling with credential-free failure tests.
extra_context: Implement the settled macOS path. Tooling implementation uses fake command runners/fixtures and needs no credentials; real credential/service use belongs to the final candidate task.
Sign CLI helpers and nested executables first, app last, with hardened runtime and secure timestamp. Use only demonstrated entitlement needs; do not recursively sign an unknown payload.

Use an explicitly supplied named Keychain profile or supported notary API credentials; the owner reports configuring luxforge-notarization for the local release. Validate it and the selected Developer ID identity during final candidate signing; never export keys, log passwords or silently select the first identity. No pull-request job receives signing secrets.

Submit the metadata-preserving ZIP with notarytool, require Accepted, retain submission result, staple/validate the app, then rearchive and compute final hashes. Keep the signed payload immutable. ZIP files cannot be stapled.
Failure keeps diagnostics and cannot downgrade into an unsigned release-ready artifact. System commands are tool wrappers, not a second project toolchain.

tasks.description: Complete the release-ready packet verifier over tag-build candidates, without duplicating the publication workflow.
extra_context: Implement candidate-contract validation without waiting for a signed artifact: use synthetic packet fixtures. Reuse existing JSON/hash/error tooling; no generalized release service or new product UI.

Ready requires matching candidate identity, final artifact hashes, source/notices review, distribution advisory disposition, signing/notary and complete required native/corpus/installation evidence. Model pending/failed/incomplete honestly; unsigned mode is rehearsal only.

Pin actions, minimize upload write permissions and prevent untrusted PR inputs from reaching credentials. Native reports bind executable identity even though the automated harness copies it into a different bundle.
Sanitize public metadata without altering private raw evidence. No private photographs, paths, coordinates or secrets in the packet; do not claim an action attestation for a local build.

A complete ready packet requires both platform artifacts and their native evidence; a qualified macOS or Linux payload alone never passes joint readiness. Hashes/source/policy apply to both targets; Apple signature/notary requirements apply only to macOS.

The tag-build workflow already builds and automatically publishes pre-release candidates after transport verification; it does not assert source/policy/native qualification. Extend readiness validation over those candidates without adding duplicate rebuild/upload/publication workflow.
